## Example 5.1 · Part (c) {#iv5-example-5-1-c .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson}

**c)** By applying the cosine rule show that $\displaystyle\cos\theta=\frac{a_xb_x+a_yb_y}{|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|}$

<div class="m-split g-proof-layout"><div data-geometric="triangle"></div><div class="g-full-proof">
<h3>From part (b)</h3>
<div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\begin{aligned}AB^2&=(b_x-a_x)^2+(b_y-a_y)^2\\&=b_x^2-2a_xb_x+a_x^2+b_y^2-2a_yb_y+a_y^2\\&=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2-2(a_xb_x+a_yb_y)\end{aligned}"></span></div>
<h3>By the cosine rule</h3>
<div class="m-equation"><span data-math="AB^2=|\underset{\sim}{a}|^2+|\underset{\sim}{b}|^2-2|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta"></span></div>
<h3>Equate, cancel and divide by <span data-math="-2|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span></h3>
<div class="m-equation"><span data-math="-2(a_xb_x+a_yb_y)=-2|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|\cos\theta"></span></div>
<div class="g-proof-answer"><div class="m-equation"><span data-math="\displaystyle\cos\theta=\frac{a_xb_x+a_yb_y}{|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|}"></span></div></div>
</div></div>
<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 5.1(c) · p. 36</div>

::: notes
The complete expansion, cosine rule, cancellation and final division are displayed. Equate the two expressions for AB²; the |a|²+|b|² terms cancel. Non-zero vectors permit division by −2|a||b|. The triangle proof uses non-collinear vectors; the parallel cases follow by direct substitution with θ=0° or 180°. Keep all parts aligned to the original scaffold.
:::
